log.msg: PROCESS SLIP, logged against myself: opened this task after already reading widely and after the coordinator's mid-task message, not before the first edit (RULE#14). No repo edit happened before this task existed — the one edit so far (report.css) landed after this file was created. Recording it anyway since the investigation phase ran long enough to look like avoidance.

BEFORE, measured with real headless renders (not the live iframe): at 1280, .ai-index-rail=474px, .page-catalog-pages=507px, both height 1110 — BESIDE (row), not stacked. At 3440, rail=613px, content=2429px, both height 1092 — also beside. Both confirm catalog.css's `@media (max-width: 64em)` column-flip (1024px) does not fire at 1280/3440 — row mode holds. Shots: scratchpad/shots/before-{rail,content}-{1280,3440}.png, before-{390,1280,3440}.png.

THE ACTUAL MATCH FOR MIKE'S WORDING: the live tab already open on the report (innerWidth 999, i.e. <64em) shows `.page-catalog` flexDirection:column, rail height 326.4px / catalog height 725.3px = 45.0% — exactly `min(34em,45%)` (ai.css:181) resolving against the container's HEIGHT once the axis flips, per that file's own comment. Rail width 731px = ~full width via align-items:stretch. That is Mike's '50/50, full width, on top' to the pixel. 1280 and 3440 do not reproduce it; something under ~1024px CSS px does.

ROOT CAUSE, PRECISE, NOT OURS TO FIX: `ext/AITask/ai.css:181` — `.page-catalog > .ai-index-rail { flex: 0 0 min(34em, 45%) }` — widens the sitewide default catalog rail (catalog.css's `--rail, 19em`) for everything under /framework/ai/. Confirmed by A/B pixel measurement below: this number is IDENTICAL before and after the render() takeover, at both 1280 and 3440. `container()` walk-up also means the report mounts beside /framework/ai/'s OWN global task rail (ai/page.js's `rail(this)`), not the day's — the day page itself has no `$pages` and already stands aside via ai.css's own `:has()` rule.

VERIFIED THE COORDINATOR'S render() OVERRIDE DOES NOT RELEASE THE RAIL — measured, not assumed. Same headless-render method, before vs after the takeover: 1280 rail 474px→474px, content 507px→507px; 3440 rail 613px→613px, content 2429px→2429px. Zero px change either width. `full` only zeroes `.page-report`'s OWN `--measure`/`--page-pad` (Page.css:47); it cannot reach an ancestor's flex-basis from the page's own file, and doesn't try to. Below 64em, re-checked on the live 999px tab post-change: flexDirection is still column, rail still 45% height / full width — UNCHANGED. The takeover does not fix the stacked state Mike is actually describing; it only changes how the report uses whatever width IT is given, at any width.

A REAL REGRESSION, FOUND AND FIXED. DesignTool's own rate()/analyze() (imported live, run in an offscreen iframe at each width — /framework/ext/DesignTool/{DesignTool.js,taste/taste.js}) on the render()-only version: 390 82/B, 1280 66/D (down from ~85/B), 1920 93/A, 3440 84/B — 0 high throughout, but the `width-used` band hit 100% (credit 0, weight 8) and `measure` scored ~0.1 (weight 10, the heaviest band) at 1280 — `.page.full` zeroing `--page-pad` to 0 means the report sits edge-to-edge with no inset at all, which the site's own taste rubric marks as filling, not using. This is exactly the 'does it use the screen or just fill it' question.

FIX, one rule, report.css only: `.page-report { padding: 3em clamp(2em, 4%, 5em) }` — the same shape as `.standard`'s own `--pad-y`/`--gutter-x`, restated locally since `full` zeroed them and this page no longer wears `.standard`. Re-measured: 390 73/C, 1280 81/B, 1920 92/A, 3440 81/B — 0 high at every width, matching or beating the pre-task baseline (73/C · 85/B · 85/B · 88/B) except 1280/3440 down a few points (still B, not a letter-grade drop) against a real gain at 1920 (85→92). `width-used` now 84–92% (was pinned to 100%) at all four widths.

SCREENSHOTS, before and after the padding fix, looked at directly: 390/1280/3440 in scratchpad/shots/before-{390,1280,3440}.png and after-fix-{390,1280,3440}.png. At 3440 the 'Five things need you' cards now run a real 4-up row using the content column's actual width, and the intro line reads as one wide sentence rather than a cramped 52em column inside a wide box — it USES the region now, not just fills it. The rail (whichever one — the day's task feed or /framework/ai/'s global one) is unchanged in width and still visually dominant at every size; that half of Mike's complaint is unresolved by anything this page's own files can do.

THE WAY BACK, checked precisely: scoping the query to `.page-report` (not the whole document, which also has unrelated 'day dashboard' text from OTHER tasks' own descriptions in the rail), both links inside the report — the opening line and the closing line of landed() — resolve to /framework/ai/2026-08-17/, correct. No console errors; 5/5 report images load (naturalWidth>0); document.visibilityState asserted visible before every shot.

GENERALISES OR NOT: special case, not a pattern to extend. The report is the one hand-authored, narrative-dashboard Page under /framework/ai/ that mixes wide image pairs, stat grids and short prose — exactly what `full` (minus its own gutter/measure) suits. Every other page under ai/ is either a day board (wants its rail for cross-task nav, `full` would be wrong) or an AITask detail view generated by shared ext/AITask machinery (no per-page page.js to add a render() override to — the fix, if any, belongs in AITask.js, fenced off today). Don't build this for them; revisit per-page if another bespoke report-shaped page shows up.

assign.outcome:
**Takeover delivered from the page's own files; the rail itself is unmoved — measured, not guessed.** `render()` (coordinator's edit, verified) plus one new rule in `report.css` — `.page-report { padding: 3em clamp(2em, 4%, 5em) }`, restating what `full` zeroed — fixed a real regression the render()-only version had: `width-used` pinned to 100% (credit 0) and `measure` scoring ~0.1, dragging 1280 to 66/D. After the fix: **0 high findings at every width**, rate() **73/C · 81/B · 92/A · 81/B** (390/1280/1920/3440) against a 73/C · 85/B · 85/B · 88/B baseline — a real gain at 1920, a few points softer at 1280/3440 but no letter-grade drop, in exchange for the page actually using its column instead of sitting edge-to-edge.

**The rail is not this page's to move.** Real pixel measurements, before vs after, at 1280 and 3440: the rail (`ext/AITask/ai.css:181`, `.ai-index-rail { flex: 0 0 min(34em, 45%) }`) claims the identical width either way — 474px and 613px respectively, 0px change. Below 64em (confirmed live at the connected tab's actual 999px width), the same rule resolves against the flipped axis and produces exactly what Mike described: rail full-width, on top, 45% of the stack's height — unchanged by anything in `report/**`. Reported, not fixed there.

**Generalises: no.** The report is the one hand-authored narrative page under `/framework/ai/`; day boards want their rail, and task-detail views are generated by shared `ext/AITask` machinery with no per-page file to patch.

Screenshots at 390/1280/3440, before and after, in the session scratchpad's `shots/` dir. Zero console errors; the day-dashboard link (both copies, inside `.page-report` specifically) still resolves to `/framework/ai/2026-08-17/`.
